planting.note: Plant container-grown specimens in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in partial shade to full sun; young trees tolerate deep shade under a forest canopy and only need more light as they mature.

directions: Real Yellowwood is South Africa's national tree, a slow-growing forest conifer with dense, glossy, broad, dark-green needle-like leaves quite unlike the narrower foliage of most other podocarps. Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in partial shade, since seedlings and young trees are true forest-floor natives that establish best under filtered light before gradually accepting more sun as they gain height. It responds well to shearing and is frequently trained as a clipped hedge, screen, or formal specimen in warm-climate gardens, in addition to being grown as a stately shade tree where space allows. Established plants are moderately drought-tolerant and largely untroubled by pests, but they have little cold tolerance and are best reserved for milder winters.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Plant container-grown specimens in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in partial shade to full sun; give this large forest tree ample overhead room to reach its eventual size.

directions: Outeniqua Yellowwood is one of Africa's tallest indigenous trees, a stately forest conifer with narrow, glossy, dark-green leaves and a distinctive tiered, pyramidal crown when young that opens into a broad, spreading canopy with age. Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in partial shade while young, since it naturally regenerates under the canopy of taller forest trees, then give it full sun as it matures into a substantial specimen or shade tree. Growth is slow, especially in its early years, but established trees are long-lived, wind-firm, and largely free of pests and disease. It has little tolerance for hard freezes and performs best in warm, frost-free or nearly frost-free gardens with consistent moisture.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)
